body:
### Summary

Since 0.13.0 made the new tar backend the default, `uv build` fails to build a wheel from an sdist created by CPython's `tarfile` (and therefore setuptools) when the file group name is 32 characters or longer.

CPython's `tarfile` fills the full 32-byte ustar `gname` field with no NUL terminator in that case. For names longer than 32 characters, it also writes the full name in a pax `gname` record. uv 0.12.24, `UV_LEGACY_TAR_BACKEND=1`, GNU tar and Python's `tarfile` all accept these archives.

We hit this in Azure Pipelines container jobs. The agent maps the host build user and its (long, domain) group into the container, so every setuptools-backed `uv build` began failing after the runner picked up 0.13.0.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
# make_sdist.py
import io, sys, tarfile

n = int(sys.argv[1])  # group name length
files = {
    "demo-0.1.0/pyproject.toml": b'[project]\nname = "demo"\nversion = "0.1.0"\n[build-system]\nrequires = ["setuptools>=77"]\nbuild-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"\n',
    "demo-0.1.0/demo/__init__.py": b"",
    "demo-0.1.0/PKG-INFO": b"Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: demo\nVersion: 0.1.0\n",
}
with tarfile.open("demo-0.1.0.tar.gz", "w:gz", format=tarfile.PAX_FORMAT) as t:
    for name, data in files.items():
        info = tarfile.TarInfo(name)
        info.size = len(data)
        info.gname = "g" * n
        t.addfile(info, io.BytesIO(data))
```

```console
$ python make_sdist.py 40
$ uvx uv@0.13.0 build --wheel demo-0.1.0.tar.gz
error: Failed to build `<tmp>/demo-0.1.0.tar.gz`
  cause: Invalid tar file
  cause: at byte 1024: invalid ustar gname field: missing NUL terminator
  cause: invalid ustar gname field: missing NUL terminator
```

### Results by group name length

| gname length | uv 0.13.0 | uv 0.13.0 + `UV_LEGACY_TAR_BACKEND=1` | uv 0.12.24 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 31 | ✅ builds | — | — |
| 32 | ❌ fails `at byte 0` | — | ✅ builds |
| 40 | ❌ fails `at byte 1024` (pax header precedes the entry) | ✅ builds | ✅ builds |

### Expected behavior

- A 32-byte `uname`/`gname` field with no NUL terminator should be accepted, as uv 0.12 did and as GNU tar and Python's `tarfile` do. CPython writes this form itself.
- When a pax `gname` record is present, it overrides the ustar field. The truncated ustar value shouldn't cause a hard failure at all.

Possibly related 0.13.0 tar-backend regression: #22492 (a different failure: hard-link members).

### Workaround

`UV_LEGACY_TAR_BACKEND=1`, or `uv build --wheel` from the source tree, which skips building an sdist.

### Platform

Windows 11 x86_64 (also reproduced in CI on Linux x86_64, Azure Pipelines container job)

### Version

uv 0.13.0 (4ecd0eff2 2026-10-09)

### Python version

Python 3.13.12
title: 0.13.0: `uv build` rejects sdists whose group name is ≥32 characters ("invalid ustar gname field: missing NUL terminator")
